nor_verger.text: Norwich Cathedral was begun in 1096 by Bishop Herbert de Losinga. The pale stone came from Caen in Normandy, shipped across the sea and up the river, then along a little canal right to the building site.
The spire is 96 metres tall, the second tallest in England after Salisbury. Our cloisters are the largest monastic cloisters in England. We don't like to boast. We just mention it every few minutes.
Edith Cavell, the Norfolk nurse who helped soldiers escape occupied Belgium and was shot for it in 1915, lies buried just outside, at Life's Green.

nor_falconer.text: Peregrine falcons nest on a platform high on the spire, every spring since 2011. The fastest animal on Earth, diving after pigeons over the Close.
There's a live camera. Half of Norwich watches the chicks hatch. The other half pretends not to.

nor_bosses.text: Look up at the vaulting. Over a thousand carved and painted bosses: Bible stories in stone, Noah's Ark, Jonah, the whole lot. Bring binoculars, everybody does.
My favourite's the one with the wrestlers. I've no idea which Bible story that is. I don't think the carver did either.
